scope: Godot player repairs, reviewer findings and native small/large-map profiling. Not blanket project certification.
comparison_notes: Same original source assets and exact recorded packets before/after. Single native GPU process, 1440x900, Compatibility, RTX 5090, VSync off. No backend benchmark ran concurrently.
Frozen baseline predates the independently tested source-byte shadow-selection correction. This tiny visual correctness change is not an optimization.
Frame intervals are inclusive callback intervals, with view context sampled at their end. Nested CPU phases overlap; do not add them. GPU timings are last available values.
Offline initialization admits the entire journal, unlike a fresh live join. Admission/preparation waiting frames can dominate its distribution.

Fixed-step playback preserves causal presentation time. Media readiness holds add wall time; all-frame percentiles must be read with held-frame counts, the non-waiting subset and sampled duration. Non-waiting context is not an exact count of advanced steps; logs give those counts.
Recorded interval excludes engine startup before the first callback and JSON/screenshot export. Cold and retained-quarter rotation stages are separate.

The frozen baseline was repeated immediately after the final client runs because earlier timings had substantial system variance. These nearby runs are the primary comparison. Raw earlier baselines remain available; none were discarded. Local measurements are not a universal speedup or hardware-independent capacity guarantee.

backend_comparison.scope: Two real current SDK games using the same authored fixture and selection strategy. Full-state cross-run normalization is INCONCLUSIVE: matching_prefixes is 0, with fresh runtime UUIDs and UUID-ordered collections producing differences even at unchanged initialization. No canonical-prefix equality is claimed. Established agreement covers all 58 command outcomes for action, behavior_id, stage, actor_name, position, HP, disclosed tile count and disclosed object count. Inclusive timing phases overlap and must not be summed; instrumentation overhead and OS scheduling apply. Dispatch excludes HTTP/polling/queue waits and packet serialization/delivery. Backend latency remains multiple seconds: after-change command P95 3946.76 ms and maximum 4760.09 ms.

remaining_limits: Large world disclosures and first construction of a camera quarter still cause visible stalls; see measured maxima.
Backend moving-light publication remains expensive; final large-room commands still have multi-second latency.
All 58 measured command-outcome fields match between backend runs. Full-state cross-game UUID normalization is inconclusive and is not claimed as parity.
Environment preparation has separately pinned residency; the 512 MiB character soft budget is not a cap on total process or GPU memory.
Long-paused prepared queues and diagnostic group histories remain unbounded. Explicit frame recording also grows until stopped.
Current light shader considers disclosed emitters per fragment; no measured GPU bottleneck justified replacing it in this pass.
Complete matching modular normal/depth assets remain deferred at the user request; no coarse whole-outfit substitution was added.

headline_comparison.basis: Adjacent frozen-baseline repeat and final runs. Earlier system conditions produced slower absolute numbers; raw earlier profiles are retained.
headline_comparison.small_steady_tradeoff: Settled median 1.086 to 1.320 ms. Explicit loading holds increase fixed-step playback wall time from 4.43 to 6.56 seconds, while initialization plus playback falls from 15.16 to 13.14 seconds.
